title: Ethiopian Harari Beef Stew
localName: የሐረሪ ሥጋ ወጥ — Ye-Harari Siga Wat
community: Harar — the ancient walled city's distinctive beef tradition
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Harari Beef Stew — the beef wat of Harar, Ethiopia's ancient walled Islamic city. Distinctly different from highland wats — influenced by Arab and Somali trading connections, with more cardamom, cinnamon, and ginger and less berbere intensity.
longDesc: The Harari beef stew reflects Harar's position as Ethiopia's most important Islamic city and a major Arab trade hub — the spice balance is more influenced by the Arab spice tradition, with aromatic spices predominating over the raw chilli heat of highland berbere.
steps: Add oil/kibbeh. Add berbere, cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves. Toast 2 minutes.
Add garlic, fresh ginger, and tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Add beef. Add water. Simmer covered 70 minutes.
chefTips: The cinnamon and cardamom distinguishes Harari stew from highland wats.
Slightly less berbere than Key Wat — the Arab spice influence moderates the heat.
commonMistakes: Too much berbere — loses the Harari character.
cookingScience: See ETH021 for general wat science. The cinnamon in the Harari stew contains cinnamaldehyde — a volatile aromatic compound that creates a warm, sweet note absent from standard Key Wat.
culturalNote: Harari beef stew is the taste of one of Africa's most ancient cities — a walled Islamic city that has been a centre of trade, scholarship, and cultural exchange for over a millennium. Its food reflects all of this history.
